```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
require(tidyverse)

kidwords = read_csv("data/kidwords/kidwords.csv", col_names = F) %>% 
  pull(X1)

orth = read_csv("data/kidwords/orth-code-kid.csv") %>% 
  mutate(orth = str_remove_all(code, "_")) %>% 
  select(-code)

phon = read_csv("data/kidwords/phon-code-kid.csv") %>% 
  mutate(phon = str_remove_all(code, "_")) %>% 
  select(-code)

all_letters = orth %>% 
  pull(orth) %>% 
  str_split(pattern = "") |>
  unlist() |>
  unique() |>
  sort()


all_phonemes = phon %>% 
  pull(phon) %>% 
  str_split(pattern = "") |>
  unlist() |>
  unique() |>
  sort()

all_phonemes

df = orth %>% 
  left_join(phon)

# 1. Define the phonological vowel symbols present in your transcription
# Add all vowel symbols used in your coding scheme (e.g., ARPAbet, CELEX, DISC, or IPA)
phon_vowels = "@^aAeEiIoOuUWY"
phon_vowel_regex <- paste0("[", phon_vowels, "].*$")

# 2. Extract bodies and rimes
df_units <- df %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Orthographic body: first vowel (a, e, i, o, u) to end
    body = str_extract(orth, "[aeiou].*$"),
    
    # Phonological rime: first vowel phoneme to end
    rime = str_extract(phon, phon_vowel_regex)
  )

# 3. Aggregate all companion words sharing the same body and rime
df_grouped <- df_units %>%
  group_by(body) %>%
  mutate(
    # All other orthographic words sharing this body
    body_matches = sapply(orth, function(w) {
      matches <- setdiff(orth, w)
      if (length(matches) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(matches, collapse = ", ")
    }),
    body_neighbor_count = n() - 1
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(rime) %>%
  mutate(
    # All other phonological words sharing this rime
    rime_matches = sapply(phon, function(p) {
      matches <- setdiff(phon, p)
      if (length(matches) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(matches, collapse = ", ")
    }),
    rime_neighbor_count = n() - 1
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(orth, phon, body, body_matches, rime, rime_matches)
```

```{r}
calculate_body_rime_metrics <- function(data, orth_col = "orth", body_col = "body", rime_col = "rime") {
  
  orth_sym <- sym(orth_col)
  body_sym <- sym(body_col)
  rime_sym <- sym(rime_col)
  
  data %>%
    # Row-wise comparison against all other rows sharing the same orthographic body
    group_by(!!body_sym) %>%
    mutate(
      # Total number of OTHER words sharing this orthographic body
      body_n = n() - 1,
      
      # Family Size: Other words sharing BOTH body AND rime (Friends)
      family_size = purrr::map_int(row_number(), function(i) {
        target_rime <- (!!rime_sym)[i]
        other_indices <- setdiff(seq_len(n()), i)
        sum((!!rime_sym)[other_indices] == target_rime)
      }),
      
      # Consistency: Friends / Total Body Neighbors (NA if no other body neighbors)
      consistency = if_else(body_n == 0, NA_real_, family_size / body_n)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# with consistency measures
df_units = calculate_body_rime_metrics(df_units) %>% 
  mutate(index = match(word, kidwords)) # add index from kidwords dataset
```



```{r write}

df_units %>% 
  filter(consistency == 1) %>% 
  write_csv(file = "data/kidwords/kidwords_with_perfect_consistency.csv")

```


# Create the samples
Note that for the consistency-based samples we are doing this in R here, but for the random samples, there is a python script in `samples.ipynb`.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
holdout_indices = read_csv("data/holdouts.csv")

holdout_indices = holdout_indices %>% 
  pull(`0...1`)



# 2. Filter eligible families:
# Exclude holdout row indices BEFORE building family clusters
eligible_families <- df_units %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(consistency),
    near(consistency, 1),
    family_size >= 2,
    !index %in% holdout_indices  # <-- Precludes holdouts
  ) %>%
  group_by(body, rime) %>%
  # Remove any holdout index that might remain, and collect
  summarise(
    indices = list(setdiff(index, holdout_indices)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pull(indices)

# 3. CRITICAL: Re-check family size >= 3
# Removing holdouts might have reduced a 3-word family down to 2 or 1 word.
# This filter keeps only families that still have at least 3 non-holdout words.
eligible_families <- eligible_families[lengths(eligible_families) >= 3]

# 4. GENERATE 10,000 SAMPLES & POPULATE BOOLEAN MATRIX
set.seed(42)

n_words_total <- nrow(df_lexicon_indexed) # All rows in original vocabulary
n_samples     <- 10000
target_words  <- 300

cat("Allocating boolean matrix (", n_words_total, "rows x", n_samples, "columns)...\n")

# Pre-allocate logical matrix filled with FALSE
bool_sample_matrix <- matrix(
  FALSE,
  nrow = n_words_total,
  ncol = n_samples,
  dimnames = list(
    paste0("word_", seq_len(n_words_total)),
    paste0("sample_", seq_len(n_samples))
  )
)

cat("Drawing 10,000 samples...\n")

# Fill matrix columns: selected row indices become TRUE
for (col_idx in seq_len(n_samples)) {
  chosen_rows <- draw_sample_indices(
    families        = eligible_families,
    target_budget   = target_words,
    min_family_size = 3
  )
  bool_sample_matrix[chosen_rows, col_idx] <- TRUE
}

# Tests
# Quick verification: ensure each column has exactly 300 TRUEs
stopifnot(all(colSums(bool_sample_matrix) == target_words))
cat("Verification passed: Every column contains exactly 300 TRUE entries.\n")

# Check that all holdout indices remain 0 across all 10,000 sample columns
holdout_check <- all(bool_sample_matrix[holdout_indices, ] == 0L)

cat("Holdouts completely excluded:", holdout_check, "\n")
# Should return: TRUE


# 4. WRITE TO FILE
storage.mode(bool_sample_matrix) <- "integer" # convert to integers from boolean

outpath <- "data/samples_consistent.csv"

write_csv(
  as.data.frame(bool_sample_matrix),
  file = outpath,
  col_names = FALSE
)

```


# Examine families sampled

```{r}

# 1. MAP WORD INDICES TO FAMILIES
# Create a unique family ID string for each word in the original vocabulary
word_family_map <- df_units %>%
  mutate(
    # Unique family identifier combining orthographic body & phonological rime
    family_id = paste(body, rime, sep = " + ")
  ) %>%
  select(index, orth, family_id)


# 2. TAKE MATRIX & EXTRACT SAMPLED FAMILIES PER SAMPLE
# Read back from the CSV:
mat <- as.matrix(read.csv(outpath, header = FALSE))

n_samples <- ncol(mat)

# Extract sampled items for each column (sample) and summarize by family
sample_family_audit_list <- vector("list", n_samples)

for (col_idx in seq_len(n_samples)) {
  # Indices where value is 1 (or TRUE)
  sampled_indices <- which(mat[, col_idx] == 1L)
  
  sample_family_audit_list[[col_idx]] <- word_family_map %>%
    filter(index %in% sampled_indices) %>%
    group_by(family_id) %>%
    summarise(
      words_sampled_in_family = n(),
      word_members = paste(orth, collapse = ", "),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(sample_id = col_idx)
}

# Combine into a single tidy dataframe
sample_family_dataset <- bind_rows(sample_family_audit_list) %>%
  select(sample_id, family_id, words_sampled_in_family, word_members)

print(head(sample_family_dataset, 10))


```

### Additional tests for the families sampled

```{r}
# 3. CHECKS
# Test 1: Exactly 300 words per sample
words_per_sample <- sample_family_dataset %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(total_words = sum(words_sampled_in_family), .groups = "drop")

stopifnot(all(words_per_sample$total_words == 300))
cat("Passed: Every sample contains exactly 300 words.\n")

# Test 2: Minimum family size constraint (no sampled family has < 3 members)
min_fam_size <- min(sample_family_dataset$words_sampled_in_family)
stopifnot(min_fam_size >= 3)
cat("Passed: All sampled families contain at least 3 members (min observed =", min_fam_size, ").\n")

# Test 3: No holdout words were sampled
if (exists("holdout_indices")) {
  holdouts_in_matrix <- sum(mat[holdout_indices, ])
  stopifnot(holdouts_in_matrix == 0)
  cat("Passed: Zero holdout words present across all 10,000 samples.\n")
}

# Test 4: Check truncation
# Distribution of family sizes present in the samples
family_size_dist <- table(sample_family_dataset$words_sampled_in_family)
cat("\nSampled family size counts:\n")
print(family_size_dist)
# Make sur eno family has fewer than three members
```
